items.label: SuperGenius mainnet implementation
items.detail: The core mainnet implementation is finished, as confirmed by project leadership. This is not a claim of a public launch, third-party security certification, or performance at production scale.

items.label: SuperGenius public mainnet
items.detail: Public activation is intentionally held until initial AI applications and integrations are ready.

items.label: Genius Cognitive System (GCS)
items.statusText: Application and integration work in progress
items.detail: GCS supplies the cognitive architecture: Semantic Core, Expert Language Models (ELMs), routing, governed memory (GAML), and verification. A documented subsystem does not by itself establish deployment status.

items.label: Genius AI Boss and other launch applications
items.detail: Application readiness and integration are prerequisites for the coordinated public launch.

items.label: GNUS token contracts on EVM networks
items.detail: Deployed EVM contracts must not be confused with activation of the native SuperGenius public mainnet. See Contracts.

notes.heading: GNUS.ai Platform Status
lines: This page distinguishes completed software implementation from public network activation and the applications being prepared for launch. It is the current release-status reference for docs.gnus.ai.

notes.heading: Why mainnet has not launched
lines: The original Q2 2026 public-launch target passed. That date is not an outstanding deadline for finishing the mainnet implementation. GNUS.ai chose to coordinate public activation with GCS, Genius AI Boss, and other applications so the network can launch with useful workloads rather than as infrastructure alone.
No revised public-launch date is announced here. Integration, validation, deployment operations, and application readiness remain distinct from mainnet code completion.

notes.heading: What “complete” does and does not establish
lines: Implementation complete means the mainnet code has reached the project's stated implementation milestone.
Publicly launched means that the native public mainnet has been activated for its intended users. This has not happened.

Audited, benchmarked, and production-proven require separate evidence: audit reports with scope and dates, measured performance on named hardware, cross-device verification tests, and actual deployment results. Implementation completion alone does not establish these.
For technical readers, distinguish three responsibilities:
GCS determines what cognitive work to perform, which experts or tools to use, what memory and policy apply, and how answers are checked.
GNUS / SuperGenius supplies the optional distributed execution, peer networking, processing, trust, and settlement infrastructure.

tracks.summary: Historical entries summarize earlier published project milestones. Their checkmarks do not by themselves establish independent audit coverage, current app count, production capacity, or public mainnet status.
